units.sourceHTML: The --show-all (-A) option acts like the -e option, except that it brackets conflicts, and it outputs all changes from older to yours, not just the unmerged changes. Thus, given the sample input files (see A Third Sample Input File), ‘diff3 -A lao tzu tao’ puts brackets around the conflict where only tzu differs:

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ (⟦1⟧) option outputs less information than the ⟦2⟧ (⟦3⟧) option, because it outputs only unmerged changes, and it never outputs the contents of the second file. Thus the ⟦4⟧ option acts like the ⟦5⟧ option, except that it brackets the first and third files from three-way overlapping changes. Similarly, ⟦6⟧ acts like ⟦7⟧, except it brackets all its (necessarily overlapping) changes. For example, for the three-way overlapping change above, the ⟦8⟧ and ⟦9⟧ options output the following:
units.sourceHTML: The --show-overlap (-E) option outputs less information than the --show-all (-A) option, because it outputs only unmerged changes, and it never outputs the contents of the second file. Thus the -E option acts like the -e option, except that it brackets the first and third files from three-way overlapping changes. units.text: If you are comparing files that have meaningless or uninformative names, you can use the ⟦0⟧ option to show alternate names in the ‘⟦1⟧’, ‘⟦2⟧’ and ‘⟦3⟧’ brackets. This option can be given up to three times, once for each input file. Thus ‘⟦4⟧’ acts like ‘⟦5⟧’, except that the output looks like it came from files named ‘⟦6⟧’, ‘⟦7⟧’ and ‘⟦8⟧’ rather than from files named ‘⟦9⟧’, ‘⟦10⟧’ and ‘⟦11⟧’.

units.sourceHTML: If you are comparing files that have meaningless or uninformative names, you can use the --label=label option to show alternate names in the ‘<<<<<<<’, ‘|||||||’ and ‘>>>>>>>’ brackets. This option can be given up to three times, once for each input file. Thus ‘diff3 -A --label X --label Y --label Z A B C’ acts like ‘diff3 -A A B C’, except that the output looks like it came from files named ‘X’, ‘Y’ and ‘Z’ rather than from files named ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’.
